sourceManifest.definition: One line per tracked file of the reviewed commit, in the order git lists them: the lowercase SHA-256 of the file, two spaces, its path, a newline. The fingerprint is the SHA-256 of these lines.

methodology: A coordinator reviewed the commit and test matrix. Three independent source reviews covered Linux confinement, memory lifetime and Unix/Windows/Apple IPC. The coordinator checked candidates against local code and operating-system contracts and kept runtime confirmations distinct from static findings.

Secret and WorkArea allocation, access, truncation, drop and flags; ClosedSecret access windows; Options, Protection, Isolation, Missing and measure reports; Worker startup, terminal variant, call, serve and drop; StackRun; fd listing and kinds; Keystroke and SecretLine; direct write_secret; platform fallbacks and all test entry points.
The inventory includes every tracked file. Runtime execution is recorded separately for each tool and target. The report uses this snapshot of the workspace procedures.

notes: The native suite started 11 unit tests and three custom integration harnesses. The suite includes bounds and wipe-on-truncation, panic propagation, mapping flags, denied calls and worker handshake tests. Its explicit self-only option case uses signal 0 for the parent and caller. A separate Landlock case uses a real signal outside the domain. The protected-stack test checks mapping flags, guard boundaries and panic propagation. It does not inspect all bytes after thread termination. The long-reply test uses 100 bytes. The host lock test checks a nonzero counter only if the crate already reports success.

The [public diagnostic](AUD-001-harnesses/README.md) observed the secretmem backend with a zero-filled sample. Whole-process locking returned true on the first call. Default re-entry returned false while the proof string still said `mlockall accepted` and `VmLck` remained 3348 kB. No sensitive data was used.

findings.title: Linux secret-memory allocation and concurrent fork share an inheritance window
findings.releaseBlockingReason: The report records whether the finding blocks the affected strict use.
findings.evidence: Static control-flow and contract review of the cited lines at the reviewed commit. The native public diagnostic identified the active backend only. No secret transfer was tested. [src/os/linux.rs line 44](../../src/os/linux.rs#L44) · [src/os/linux.rs line 57](../../src/os/linux.rs#L57) · [src/os/linux.rs line 74](../../src/os/linux.rs#L74) · [src/os/unix.rs line 33](../../src/os/unix.rs#L33) · [OS or language contract](https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man2/memfd_secret.2.html) · [OS or language contract](https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man2/mlock.2.html)
findings.expected: Child exclusion must hold for a buffer reported out of children.
findings.observed: During successful secretmem allocation, the shared backing file is temporarily open across fork. DONTFORK affects a mapping and CLOEXEC takes effect at exec. Neither revokes an already inherited descriptor. A concurrent fork without immediate exec can retain the same backing object into which the parent later places secret bytes. The private anonymous fallback has different sharing semantics. The diagnostic confirmed use of secretmem on the host, without testing disclosure.
findings.recommendedFix: Use the private anonymous backend when fork can run concurrently. Reserve shared secretmem for a fork-free worker or a caller with an enforceable fork-free lifecycle. Make this precondition part of the guarantee.
findings.requiredVerification: Check both backends, allocation lifecycle and process model using public fixtures on supported Linux kernels. Verify the claimed scope before accepting sensitive input.

findings.title: Unix worker acknowledges isolation after incomplete descriptor cleanup
findings.releaseBlockingReason: The report records whether the finding blocks the affected strict use.
findings.evidence: Static control-flow and contract review of the cited lines at the reviewed commit. [src/os/unix.rs line 252](../../src/os/unix.rs#L252) · [src/os/unix.rs line 264](../../src/os/unix.rs#L264) · [src/os/unix.rs line 274](../../src/os/unix.rs#L274) · [src/worker.rs line 150](../../src/worker.rs#L150)
findings.expected: A worker advertising clean inherited channels must know that all unintended descriptors were closed.
findings.observed: After the bulk close fails or is unavailable, directory-open failure silently returns, directory-entry errors are discarded and close results are ignored. Startup still sends the protection bits. If the worker inherited a writable file or socket and fallback enumeration fails, the strict handshake can accept secrets with the channel still present. The normal Linux close_range path is unaffected.
findings.recommendedFix: Propagate the cleanup outcome before sending the handshake. Use a supported close-from operation or a verified fallback, with explicit handling of the listing descriptor and OS close semantics.
findings.requiredVerification: Verify clean startup and startup refusal on incomplete cleanup with public descriptors, including the fallback on macOS.

findings.title: Linux tracer evidence for one thread is reported process-wide
findings.releaseBlockingReason: The report records whether the finding blocks the affected strict use.
findings.evidence: Static control-flow and contract review of the cited lines at the reviewed commit. [src/os/linux.rs line 140](../../src/os/linux.rs#L140) · [src/os/linux.rs line 282](../../src/os/linux.rs#L282) · [src/os/linux.rs line 775](../../src/os/linux.rs#L775) · [src/protect.rs line 241](../../src/protect.rs#L241) · [OS or language contract](https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man2/ptrace.2.html)
findings.expected: A positive process-wide result requires evidence covering prior tracers on all relevant threads.
findings.observed: TracerPid is read only for the calling thread. Setting the process non-dumpable restricts new access and does not detach existing tracers. Linux ptrace attaches per thread. A multithreaded caller can pass a required NoMemoryReading check despite an existing tracer of a different thread sharing its memory. The single-threaded worker avoids this particular mismatch.
findings.recommendedFix: Establish the property before concurrency, or implement a sound process-wide check under a controlled thread lifecycle. Otherwise mark it unverified for a multithreaded caller.
findings.requiredVerification: Cover single-thread initialization, multithread scope and unavailable thread inventory. A process-wide positive result must refer to the entire claimed scope.

findings.title: Windows worker pipe ends are briefly inheritable by unrelated launches
findings.releaseBlockingReason: The report records whether the finding blocks the affected strict use.
findings.evidence: Static control-flow and contract review of the cited lines at the reviewed commit. [src/os/windows.rs line 855](../../src/os/windows.rs#L855) · [src/os/windows.rs line 919](../../src/os/windows.rs#L919) · [src/os/windows.rs line 962](../../src/os/windows.rs#L962) · [src/os/windows.rs line 987](../../src/os/windows.rs#L987) · [OS or language contract](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/procthread/inheritance)
findings.expected: Only the designated worker and its parent may hold secret request and response pipe handles.
findings.observed: Both ends are created inheritable. Inheritance is cleared later on the parent ends. The explicit handle list limits inheritance for the worker launch only. A separate child spawned concurrently by the same parent using broad handle inheritance can receive an IPC endpoint. This applies to applications with such process-launch behavior. No Windows runtime observation.
findings.recommendedFix: Keep inheritable ends in a dedicated launch broker with controlled child creation, or enforce coordinated allowlisted inheritance across all launchers in the process. Creating parent ends non-inheritable also narrows the window.
findings.requiredVerification: Validate handle ownership during concurrent independent benign launches on Windows. Verify only designated actors can own the IPC endpoints.

findings.title: macOS accepts local probe denials without a confirmed sandbox profile
findings.releaseBlockingReason: The report records whether the finding blocks the affected strict use.

findings.expected: A strict, process-wide file or network restriction requires confirmation of the intended profile or independently equivalent policy.
findings.observed: The result of sandbox_init is used only to free an error message. A permission denial creating one temporary file can come from its directory. A single UDP loopback check likewise cannot characterize an unknown profile. findings.requiredVerification: On macOS verify first success, repeat entry, and refused installation with independently restricted probe locations in disposable processes.

findings.title: Signal-domain isolation can satisfy a stricter self-only claim
findings.releaseBlockingReason: The report records whether the finding blocks the affected strict use.
findings.evidence: Static control-flow and contract review of the cited lines at the reviewed commit. [src/os/linux.rs line 150](../../src/os/linux.rs#L150) · [src/os/linux.rs line 170](../../src/os/linux.rs#L170) · [src/os/linux.rs line 223](../../src/os/linux.rs#L223) · [src/os/linux.rs line 624](../../src/os/linux.rs#L624) · [src/protect.rs line 272](../../src/protect.rs#L272) · [OS or language contract](https://docs.kernel.org/userspace-api/landlock.html)
findings.expected: Evidence must distinguish self-only addressing, a Landlock domain boundary and unsupported enforcement.
findings.observed: A successful seccomp installation plus Landlock ABI support can stand in for a failed Landlock application. An enforced Landlock signal scope groups processes. The self-only filter separately embeds the installing process ID, which is inherited across fork. A required ForeignSignalsRefused result can mean separate things and can be positive without the advertised restriction. A child cannot interpret an inherited fixed-ID filter as its own self-only policy.
findings.recommendedFix: Distinguish confirmed signal-domain scope from self-only mode, track enforcement separately from availability, and bind or restrict the supported process lifecycle.
findings.requiredVerification: Test each enforcement state independently, including unavailable Landlock, repeated entry and supported descendant semantics. Verify the strict requirement accepts only the requested property.

findings.title: Unsupported speculation control is accepted as confirmed mitigation
findings.releaseBlockingReason: The report records whether the finding blocks the affected strict use.
findings.evidence: Static control-flow and contract review of the cited lines at the reviewed commit. [src/os/linux.rs line 259](../../src/os/linux.rs#L259) · [src/os/linux.rs line 272](../../src/os/linux.rs#L272) · [src/protect.rs line 257](../../src/protect.rs#L257) · [OS or language contract](https://docs.kernel.org/userspace-api/spec_ctrl.html)
findings.expected: A positive mitigation claim needs a confirmed protection or a supported indication that the CPU is unaffected.
findings.observed: For indirect branches the implementation accepts ENODEV. The kernel defines it as an unsupported selector, while a successful zero return identifies an unaffected CPU. The code also groups ordinary disable with irreversible disable. The strict requirement or detailed report can overstate speculative-execution mitigation on particular architectures and configurations. No leakage was observed.
findings.recommendedFix: Represent unsupported as unknown and distinguish reversible from permanent disable where the public contract promises permanence. Permit platform-specific equivalents only with evidence.
findings.requiredVerification: Validate the mapping from independent kernel results to supported, unaffected, reversible, irreversible and unknown statuses.

findings.title: Protected stack properties cannot be required before secret work
findings.releaseBlockingReason: The report records whether the finding blocks the affected strict use.
findings.evidence: Static control-flow and contract review of the cited lines at the reviewed commit. [src/stack.rs line 12](../../src/stack.rs#L12) · [src/os/unix.rs line 170](../../src/os/unix.rs#L170) · [src/os/unix.rs line 184](../../src/os/unix.rs#L184) · [src/os/unix.rs line 358](../../src/os/unix.rs#L358) · [src/os/unix.rs line 391](../../src/os/unix.rs#L391)
findings.expected: A caller relying on exclusion or locking must verify those properties before invoking its callback.
findings.observed: Page advice and locking are best effort. Apple explicitly reports no per-mapping dump exclusion. The callback runs before the caller receives even the lock result. Dump and child flags are omitted from StackRun. findings.recommendedFix: Provide a pre-callback required-properties policy and report the mapping outcomes. Identify when a separately confirmed process-wide measure supplies an equivalent guarantee.
findings.requiredVerification: On Linux and Apple assert that missing required flags prevent callback entry. Test the best-effort API and normal/panic completion separately.

findings.title: Stack wiping assumes every post-pthread byte is an initialized Rust u8
findings.releaseBlockingReason: The report records whether the finding blocks the affected strict use.
findings.evidence: Static control-flow and contract review of the cited lines at the reviewed commit. [src/os/unix.rs line 379](../../src/os/unix.rs#L379) · [src/os/unix.rs line 386](../../src/os/unix.rs#L386) · [src/os.rs line 105](../../src/os.rs#L105) · [OS or language contract](https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/slice/fn.from_raw_parts_mut.html)
findings.expected: Final wiping must be valid for arbitrary used stack memory and may begin only once all thread access has ended.
findings.observed: The code forms a mutable slice of initialized bytes over an entire used stack. Arbitrary frames can contain uninitialized storage or padding even though the original mapping was zero-filled. pthread_join's return value is discarded. The unsafe conversion lacks an initialization proof for a safe public API. Successful ordinary tests do not establish this invariant. No optimizer-induced leak was observed.
findings.recommendedFix: Use a write-only raw wipe or a MaybeUninit byte representation with an optimization-resistant wipe. Establish successful join before releasing the backing allocation and job.
findings.requiredVerification: Review lifetime and initialization invariants, check generated wipe code, and exercise normal and panic paths on supported Unix runtimes.

findings.title: ClosedSecret forgets the previous access mode after a refused reseal
findings.releaseBlockingReason: The report records whether the finding blocks the affected strict use.
findings.evidence: Static control-flow and contract review of the cited lines at the reviewed commit. [src/protect/closed.rs line 112](../../src/protect/closed.rs#L112) · [src/protect/closed.rs line 135](../../src/protect/closed.rs#L135) · [src/protect/closed.rs line 144](../../src/protect/closed.rs#L144)
findings.expected: A mutable reference or destructor wipe requires confirmed write access, including after OS protection failures.
findings.observed: A read-only opening followed by refused resealing leaves the closed boolean false. A subsequent refused read-write transition can therefore be ignored even if the mapping is still read-only. When OS policy refuses both transitions, a write or cleanup can fault. The condition does not establish disclosure and was not observed on this host.
findings.recommendedFix: Track actual access permissions explicitly and distinguish unsupported backends. Refuse any operation whose required access cannot be established before producing the reference or wiping.
findings.requiredVerification: Exercise policy-refused transitions from read-only state, including drop and callback unwinding, with public data.

findings.title: Dropping a worker can wait forever after rejecting a large reply
findings.releaseBlockingReason: The report records whether the finding blocks the affected strict use.
findings.evidence: Static control-flow and contract review of the cited lines at the reviewed commit. [src/worker.rs line 112](../../src/worker.rs#L112) · [src/worker.rs line 125](../../src/worker.rs#L125) · [src/worker.rs line 173](../../src/worker.rs#L173) · [src/os/unix.rs line 243](../../src/os/unix.rs#L243) · [src/os/windows.rs line 785](../../src/os/windows.rs#L785) · [OS or language contract](https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man7/pipe.7.html)
findings.expected: A rejected, oversized answer should permit prompt disposal and reaping of the worker.
findings.observed: The parent rejects the advertised size, retains the unread output pipe, closes only the input and waits. The child can be blocked writing the rest of a legitimate answer. findings.requiredVerification: Use a normal large public response with a bounded test deadline on Unix and Windows. Verify prompt return and child reaping.

findings.title: Fork-based work inside a protected stack may lose its active stack
findings.releaseBlockingReason: The report records whether the finding blocks the affected strict use.

[src/os/unix.rs line 170](../../src/os/unix.rs#L170) · [src/os/unix.rs line 183](../../src/os/unix.rs#L183) · [src/os/unix.rs line 220](../../src/os/unix.rs#L220) · [src/os/unix.rs line 358](../../src/os/unix.rs#L358)
findings.expected: The callback contract should identify supported ways to launch children safely.
findings.observed: The active stack is configured to be wiped or excluded on fork. limitations: Native runtime evidence is limited to Linux x86_64 on kernel 7.0.0-43-generic. Clippy type-checked other targets. No native Windows, macOS, iOS, Android or WASM runtime, installer, link test or end-to-end consuming application was exercised.

The ordinary suite, diagnostic and code review do not certify complete memory erasure, impossibility of disclosure, or resistance to privileged OS access. No secret transfer or exploit was demonstrated. No formal proof, sanitizer or disassembly campaign was performed.
The host used a fresh target directory and offline locked dependencies. Upstream dependency internals and current transitive advisories were not audited.
Terminal password input integration in MHFE, actual StegoCode integration, browser UI, suspend images, VM snapshots and device-wide crash collectors are outside the library tests.
remediationNote: All findings are open against the reviewed commit. No fixes or fix-verification commits were made. A blocker in the register applies to integrations relying on the affected guarantee. Address the five high-severity boundary failures first. Verify required flags, stack entry and unsafe cleanup before enabling their strict profiles.
integrationGuidance: Use a fresh single-threaded, fork-free worker where the platform supports one. Verify required protections and intended channel ownership before admitting test or user secrets. Mobile integrations need their own platform-specific isolation and device evidence.

Protect long-lived secrets and Argon2 work areas explicitly. Determine whether a given allocation fits the lock quota. A strict configuration that requires locked work memory must refuse the sensitive operation when it cannot obtain it. Keep whole-process locking opt-in.

The current worker protocol accepts a u32 byte count and makes a non-fallible allocation on the receiving side. Define application-specific request/reply maxima, use fallible allocation for untrusted sizes, and retire broken transports on partial I/O.
Measure names should distinguish socket creation, usable network connections, and inherited channels. A token capability check is evidence about policy, not an observed network connection test.
Forked descendants should not reuse copied protected-buffer objects or cached lock flags. Memory locks are not inherited and mappings can be wiped or absent.

Verify the integration against native OS crash handling. Windows reports no whole-process NoCoreDumps and Windows Error Reporting can retain stacks and registers. WASM offers buffer wiping only. SIGKILL and abort do not execute Rust Drop. Hibernation and VM snapshots require OS policy.
